decisions.reason: Requesting a more robust text-entry representation does not change the independent requirement that the placeholder clear when the field is activated.
The architecture-quality change does not remove or alter the requirement for interactive-field help labels.
A more robust field representation does not itself change the required formatting-retention behavior of the Title field.
The source requests a more robust field architecture but does not select, remove, or otherwise resolve the visible cue used to identify editable fields.
The source concerns the representation of text-entry fields, not the workflow or stability of copying content from legacy templates.
The field-architecture change does not entail any change to manual line-break behavior after pasted content.
The source does not discuss or alter bullet sizing, alignment, balance, color, or visual design.
The requested text-entry architecture change does not affect the independently defined Tab-based list hierarchy.
The source does not change the supported Word environment or the general requirement for stable rendering across users.
Changing the architecture of text-entry fields does not entail a change to pasted-table or column-containment behavior.
The source does not establish any change to style-name prefixes or their applicability.
The request for a more robust text-entry representation does not modify the prescribed style catalog or its deployment across templates.
